agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Order (April 22,
2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be
publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be live
streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to bsaleaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency,
as well as states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of
California, and a federal emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to
reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but
conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees. This way the public, the staff, and the Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which are
not listed on the agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action
may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing
response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak during the
meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration.
Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to
the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar
will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first
will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow
the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above
are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
bsaleaumua@malibucitv.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for
the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please contact Environmental Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229.
Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure
accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II]. Requests for use of audio or video
equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to Alex Montano at (310) 456-2489, ext. 227,
or amontano@malibucity.org before 12:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.

   Parks and Recreation Commission

  In response to Chair Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the bulky items were

  In response to Chair Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the bi-annual site

  B.  Sunscreen Station Program
  Recommended Action: Review the BrightGuard Sunscreen Station Program and
  provide direction to staff.

  Recreation Manager Gallo presented the staff report.

  Alexander Beck provided information on the sunscreen station program and
  BrightGuard's partnership with UCLA Health. He stated the cancer prevention
  program was for Malibu residents and visitors.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Gallo stated the
  BrightGuard proposal included the installation of sunscreen stations at Malibu
  Bluffs Park, Legacy Park, Las Flores Park, Trancas Canyon Park, Equestrian Park,
  Legacy Park, and the Malibu Community Pool. She stated staff recommended
  installing sunscreen stations at two supervised facilities, Malibu Bluffs Park and
  the Malibu Community Pool.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Gallo stated she
  worked with Mr. Beck to provide sunscreen stations similar to hand sanitizing
  stations. She stated BrightGuard's proposed stations violated regulations in the
  Malibu Municipal Code.

  Chair Peak suggested a sunscreen station at Trancas Canyon Park.

  Commissioner Jenner indicated agreement with Chair Peak and suggested
  installing it inside the restrooms.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of May I 7, 2022
  Page 4 of 6

  Chair Peak stated installation could occur from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Gallo stated
  BrightGuard would be responsible for maintenance, weekly monitoring, and
  refilling the stations for the duration of the Agreement.

  Mr. Beck stated he hoped the program could continue for multiple years in Malibu.
  He stated he worked with the City of Santa Monica from Memorial Day to Labor
  Day, and the program temporarily shut down for two years due to COVID-19.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Mr. Beck stated UCLA Health funds the
  program, and the sunscreen was not available over the counter.

  In response to Chair Peak, Mr. Beck stated the City of Santa Monica had sunscreen
  stations at various locations from 2017 to 2019, and there were few instances of
  vandalism. He stated he would remove sunscreen stations that were vandalized
  more than two times.

  Chair Peak recommended staff work with Mr. Beck to install sunscreen stations at
  Trancas Canyon Park, Malibu Bluffs Park, and the Malibu Community Pool.

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Jenner seconded a motion to
  install two sunscreen stations at Malibu Bluffs Park, one sunscreen station at the
  Malibu Community Pool, and one sunscreen station at Trancas Canyon Park from
  July I through September 5, 2022. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0, Commissioner Guldimann absent.

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department during May 2022.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in May 2022.

RECREATION

Aquatics: The Malibu Aquatics Foundation Seawolves Swim Team and Adult Masters
Conditioning summer programs took place from May 15 to July 31. Seventy-two
participants registered for the program.

The Community Services Department hosted a Red Cross Lifeguard Certification Course
on May 21 and 22 at the Malibu Community Pool. Katherine Mutchler, Pool Manager at
Pepperdine University, taught the hybrid course. Thirteen participants completed the class
and were encouraged to apply for seasonal work with the City at the Malibu Community
Pool.

Community Classes: Afterschool programs in partnership with the Malibu Boys and Girls
Club concluded the week of May 23 at Malibu Elementary School and Webster Elementary
School. Programs included soccer, Spanish, and theater for 75 students.

Spring community classes held at Malibu Bluffs Park concluded on May 31 , including
cartooning , chess, hip hop, adult dance, soccer, Music Together, parent and me yoga,
and parent and me soccer.

  Page 1 of 4  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 Day Camps: Registration for Summer Day Camps opened on May 9. Over 350
participants, ages 5 through 14, pre-registered for enrichment, skateboarding, sports, and
surf camps that begin June 13.

Outdoor Recreation:  Recreation staff led a Family Adventure Hike at Charmlee
Wilderness Park on May 7. Thirteen participants learned about the park's terrain, native
edible flowers, and insects.

Recreation staff led a Sunset Hike at Charmlee Wilderness Park on May 18. Nine
participants hiked to the vista to view the setting sun.

Seniors: Weekly Senior recreation programs continued in the Senior Center, with
additional class offerings, including ballet, tap dance, and bridge. Existing programs
include Art Trek, Cardio Salsa, Chair Yoga, Knitting, Mat Yoga, Gentle Mat Pilates, Relax
through Coloring, and Stretch and Strength.

On May 5, Recreation staff hosted a Build Your Own Flower Bouquet activity to celebrate
Mother's Day. Over 30 seniors attended the event and assembled a bouquet with fresh
flowers, wrapping paper, ribbon, and gift tags.

Over 670 Seniors received a copy of the June Senior Center Monthly Newsletter in the
mail. The June Newsletter featured a Kickoff to Summer Senior Lunch at Malibu Bluffs
Park.

The Senior Center was closed from May 25 through June 10 for the Malibu Regional Vote
Center in the California Primary Election. All Senior Center classes and programs
continued, with many being relocated to Malibu Bluffs Park. The Computer Lab remained
open, and staff was available to assist with Dial-A-Ride and other services.

Skate Programs: The spring Learn to Skate program, instructed by Champ Camp for
children ages 6 to 12, concluded on May 15. The session reached a maximum capacity of
17 participants. Instructors subdivided the group based on ability and skate technique.

The Girls Skateboarding Clinic, instructed by Champ Camp, was held on May 22 with a
maximum capacity of 15 participants. The clinic is part of the "Play Like A Girl Malibu"
program to encourage female sports participation.

Social Media: Department social media featured summer programs, art exhibitions,
employment opportunities, and Senior Center programs. Social media analytics show that
the primary audience is Malibu residents, ages 35 through 44.

Special Events: The Department hosted a summer-themed Park Tales at Malibu Bluffs
Park in partnership with the Malibu Library on May 26. Twenty-five families received a
goodie bag with City program flyers, snacks, sunglasses, a rainbow windmill, and a book
donated by the Malibu Library.
  Page 2 of 4  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Over 75 car enthusiasts attended Cars and Coffee at Malibu Bluffs Park on May 8 and 22.

Sports: The spring youth basketball program concluded on May 7 with 20 participants,
ages 4 through 14. Breakthrough Sports instructed the outdoor program at Malibu High
School. The soccer, tennis, and volleyball programs continued through the first week of
June.

PARK MAINTENANCE

Charmlee Wilderness Park: Trail crews completed Priority Area 1 weed clearance and
began Priority Area 2.

Staff completed an assessment of all park trails and removed graffiti from multiple rocks.

Staff met with Los Angeles County Waterworks staff at the Charmlee Park pump station
to complete the annual backflow testing.

Las Flores Park: Removed graffiti on the exterior wall of the restroom building.

Legacy Park: Began weed abatement at the leach field area near Supercare Pharmacy.

Removed tree roots intruding within a three-foot section of drainage pipe from the drinking
fountain. The removal was completed to prevent future drainage issues.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Removed graffiti from the concrete pavement and retaining wall near
the whale watch station and various picnic tables throughout the park with the power
washer.

Replaced a damaged section of the temporary skate park surfacing with new Skatelite
and wood screws to secure the replacements. Additionally, the wood railing near the steps
to the bowl area was also repaired.

Removed a dirt blockage in the drinking fountain drain located at the Major Baseball field.

Installed and replaced two faulty cam locks on the events bin display case.

Malibu City Hall: Repaired damaged drip irrigation in two parking lot planters.

Medians and Parkways: Staff met with contractors and the Public Works Superintendent
to inspect damage to electrical and water lines at the triangle planter at Civic Center Way
and Malibu Canyon Road. Repairs are expected to take place throughout June.

  Page 3 of 4  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 Trancas Canyon Park: Repaired an underground drainage pipe for one of the drinking
fountains that was damaged by nearby tree roots.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

Subject:  Youth Sports Organizations and Facility Use

RECOMMENDED ACTION : Receive and file a report regarding local youth sports
organization registration data and facility use.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department works with local youth sports
organizations throughout the year to provide field space for practices and games at Malibu
Bluffs Park. Additionally, the City maintains annual Facility Use Agreements with Malibu
American Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO) and Malibu Little League (MLL), who are
the primary users of field space apart from City-organized programs.

Malibu AYSO
AYSO's regular season takes place from August to November for children ages 4 to 17.
In 2021-2022, AYSO had 386 registered participants. The percentage of non-resident
participants is approximately 10% of the total number of registered participants.

  Season  Registered Participants
  2017-2018  519
  2018-2019  475
  2019-2020  466
  2020-2021  Clinic only due to COVID-19
  2021-2022  386

For the 2022-2023 regular season , AYSO will use Malibu Bluffs Park for practices and
games seven days a week. Following the regular season, AYSO will transition to their
playoffs and all-star season beginning the week after Thanksgiving and continuing through
February. The weekly field space usage during the playoffs and all-star seasons will be
approximately 40%-50% of the regular season. Additionally, AYSO hosts spring soccer
  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item #5.A.
 during their off-season from March through May with practices and games on Sundays at
Malibu Bluffs Park.

Malibu Little League
MLL Baseball and Softball serves the Malibu area and has strict residency guidelines for
registration. Families must reside in the Malibu region or apply for a special permit to
participate. In 2022, MLL consisted of 199 Malibu players and 55 non-resident players.

  MLL Season  Reaistered Participants
  2017  200
  2018  167
  2019  115
  2020  Canceled (COVID-19)
  2021  194
  2022  254

MLL installs temporary backstops on the Multipurpose Field at Malibu Bluffs Park to
increase the amount of available field space for younger players and games. During their
2022 season, MLL offered Coach Pitch Baseball for the second consecutive year and
Juniors Baseball (formerly Pony Baseball) for the first time. The new programs increased
their registration numbers by 59 players.

MLL's regular season begins each February and continues through July, with all-star
practices following the regular season. MLL uses field space during the regular season for
practices and games seven days a week.

Additionally, MLL offers fall baseball during their off season from September to November.
Practices and games take place at Malibu Bluffs Park five days a week.

City-Organized Programs
The City organizes several youth sports programs throughout the year at Malibu Bluffs Park,
including:

  Proaram  Months  Aaes
  Flaa Football Proaram  September to November  7 - 10
  Girls Sports Clinics  Quarterly  8 - 13
  Parent and Me Soccer  January to December  1-2
  Parent and Me T-Ball  March to Auaust  1-2
  Youth Soccer Proaram  Januarv to December  3-5

The City also hosts Summer and Fall Adult Softball Leagues on Sundays from June to
November each year, utilizing the Pony Field at Malibu Bluffs Park.

  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item #5.A.
 Summary of Field Use
In 2022, organized youth sports field usage during their respective primary seasons
remained consistent with 2021. Off-season usage by MLL increased by two days a week
compared to 2021, due to increased opportunities for youth to focus on a specific sport
year-round.

Due to limited field space, AYSO and MLL have adjusted their schedules and compressed
teams to use available space during both their primary and off- seasons while factoring
various limitations, including:

  •  Limited hours of daylight during the spring, fall, and winter
  •  Varying age ranges require different amounts of practice space
  •  Additional annual special events, facility reservations, and field renovations

Fields at Malibu Bluffs Park are currently reserved at maximum capacity with youth sports
leagues and City programs, resulting in few options to accommodate new programs or
additional reservations.
